name: Direct Counter 4-4-2

slots.why: Distributes quickly to the wingers or forwards to start the break.
Support full-back stays reasonably back, but supplies width when the counter is on.
Central defender. Cover is the alternate.
Cover centre-back sweeps behind his partner, which suits a deeper block; Defend is the alternate.
Winger (Support) is a quick outlet who receives the ball wide and runs at the defence.
Defensive central midfielder breaks up play and shields the back four.
Box-to-box midfielder is the runner who supports the forwards on the break.
Winger (Support) on the right, doing the same job as on the left.
Deep-lying forward (or Complete Forward) holds up the ball so the others can arrive.
Advanced Forward runs in behind the defence. Poacher is the alternate.

description: A compact 4-4-2 that accepts periods without the ball and attacks space quickly after regaining possession.
whyGood: The DLF provides an outlet while the AF and wide runners attack the space left by an advanced opponent.
whyThisShape: A flat 4-4-2 that sits in a mid-to-low block and breaks quickly when it wins the ball, using its two wingers, a runner from midfield and two forwards. It is the simplest way to counter-attack: few players stay forward, so the rest can defend.
whenToUse: Against a stronger or possession-based team that will leave space behind its defence, when you have quick wingers and forwards.
whenNotToUse: Against a team that sits deep and does not leave space to run into, since the counter has nothing to attack.

instructionRationale.Slightly More Direct Passing: Gets the ball forward to the outlets quicker after winning it.
instructionRationale.Higher Tempo: Speeds up the break so the defence has no time to reorganise.
instructionRationale.Pass Into Space: Plays the ball behind the defence for the runners.
instructionRationale.Counter: Attacks straight away on winning the ball.
instructionRationale.Regroup: Falls back into shape after losing the ball, before the next break.
instructionRationale.Lower Line of Engagement: Lets the opponent have the ball in their own half, which leaves the space to counter into.
instructionRationale.Standard Defensive Line: A balanced line keeps the block compact without giving up too much space in behind.
